turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the screen's having a moment. Right. What's brought you in?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh it's fine, I was reading the posters. Um, I've been absolutely knackered for ages. Proper wiped out, not just a late night.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long's the tiredness been going on?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Err, about three months? Maybe a bit longer. I can't pin the day down, it sort of crept up. I did think it was just the dark mornings.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any shortness of breath?

[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. Two flights up to the flat and I'm puffed, have to stop on the landing. Sitting down I'm fine. The bus this morning was a nightmare, some bloke and a dog, but that's not why I'm here.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry. The stairs bit again? I clicked the wrong tab.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Two flights, breathless, stop halfway. Fine once I sit down.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any odd cravings?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Cravings? No. Don't think so.

[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, actually, um, I've been crunching ice all evening, every evening, a whole tray of it. My flatmate thinks I've lost the plot. We were watching that baking thing and I just sat there with a bowl of ice.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ice, right. You're vegetarian, according to this?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Strict, yeah. No meat, no fish, not since uni. Eggs and cheese are fine, I'm not vegan. I nearly went vegan after a podcast but I couldn't give up cheese.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): Are your periods heavy?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No, they're normal. Regular, every month, about five days, not heavy, same as always.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chest pain? Heart racing?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No chest pain. Heart doesn't race.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): Medicines? Slowly, I'm typing.

[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, desogestral, the mini pill, 75 micrograms, one every morning, for contraception. I tried ferrus sulphate last year, the 200 milligram tablets, but I stopped after a fortnight cos my tummy hated it.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): Allergies to anything?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): Family, anyone with anything? It beeped, sorry, go on.

[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, my dad got diabetes in his fifties, type two I think. Mum didn't have any of that, she's fine. My older sister's got blood pressure but no sugar. And my grandad on dad's side had a heart attack when he was about seventy.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Work, food, exercise, alcohol?

[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): I work in a bookshop, part time, about twenty hours a week, afternoons mostly. Strict vegetarian, no meat or fish. I walk to the shop sometimes but no proper exercise, no gym. A glass of wine on a Saturday, and I don't smoke.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Blood tests before, for this?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, last year, at the uni health centre. They said my iron was borderline. I never got an actual number, and I can't remember if it was March or later, the date's gone.
[SEG0028] person_3 (NURSE): Sorry to butt in. Obs from just now, blood pressure 112 over 74, pulse 82, sats 98 percent.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ta. Tiredness, the ice, breathless on the stairs, vegetarian. I think this is most likely low iron. That's a working impression, not confirmed till the bloods are back.

[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): So we'll do a full blood count, ferritin, vitamin B12 and folate. The nurse takes the bloods Thursday morning. No need to fast, just don't take any vitamin tablets that morning.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Thursday's alright, I don't start till eleven. I'll bring a book, the queue's always grim.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): If those come back borderline we'll add a coeliac screen. If the breathlessness doesn't settle once the iron's dealt with, then a chest x-ray. Not booking that now.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Lentils, beans, dark green veg, and orange juice or vitamin C alongside, helps the iron absorb. I'll see you in two weeks with the results.
[SEG0034] person_3 (NURSE): Thursday, half eight, phlebotomy. Leave the vitamins till after, like he said.

spec.situation: Tired young woman, strict vegetarian, breathless on stairs, craving ice; periods normal by her account; blood tests planned; diet advice.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

features: test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Prior iron test is supported, but transcript says last year's test was at uni health centre, not completed now.

omissions.text: Breathlessness detail omitted: she becomes breathless after two flights of stairs and has to stop halfway/on the landing; she is fine at rest/sitting down.
Ice craving detail omitted: she is crunching ice every evening, about a whole tray.
Menstrual history detail omitted: periods are regular every month, about five days, and unchanged/same as always.
Ferrous sulfate was stopped because it caused gastrointestinal upset ('my tummy hated it').
Previous investigation/history omitted: last year at the university health centre she was told her iron was 'borderline'.
Investigation status recorded wrongly: the prior 'iron blood test' was not completed in this consultation; only a past outside test was mentioned, while current blood tests are planned for Thursday.
